traits.note: FNA vol. 28, Kindbergia (Ignatov; efloras, read 2026-11-06): plants medium-sized to large, in loose to dense mats, occasionally tufts, green, yellow-green or brownish; stems creeping, ascending to erect, regularly pinnate; seta red-brown, roughened; capsule inclined to horizontal, red-brown, short-ovate, curved; operculum long-rostrate; dioicous. Typical values are K. oregana, the Oregon beaked moss (same volume, p. 447): plants large, plumose; stems 10-25(-45) cm; branches 6-10 mm, almost always simple; branch leaves plicate, 1-2 x (0.6-)0.7-0.9(-1.2) mm; seta 1.5-2 cm; on litter, soil rich in humus and rotten logs in forests, mesic, diffusely lighted places, 0-1300 m, B.C. to California.

traits.height_typical_m.note: The depth of a mat of ascending stems 10-25 cm long (FNA): a few centimetres. Estimate.

traits.light.note: FNA vol. 28, Kindbergia oregana (efloras, read 2026-11-06): forests, in diffusely lighted places: part shade to shade, not open ground.

traits.capsule_share.note: Dioicous; capsules frequent on the species in PNW forests. Estimate.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Large plumose shoots 10-25 cm long that creep and branch: it spreads faster than the wall mats (Hypnum 0.012). Estimate; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hue measured: imagekit run moss-colour-2026-11-05 on batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05 (iNaturalist research-grade photos from Washington, script moss_colour.py), Kindbergia oregana, 24 photos: the median of each photo's linear r/g 0.80 and b/g 0.26. Photos are exposed brighter than moss is, so only the hue is taken from them; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, as the other moss genera's colours take it (a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible; see Hypnum's note).
